sections.html:
The Register of Deeds sits on the ground-level floor of the Martin County Governmental Building in Williamston. Land records there start in 1771. Easements, agreements, assignments, releases, plats, deeds and deeds of trust are all recorded at this counter, with an index for each kind and a separate index for plats.

Uniform commercial code statements join the real estate books too, a practice dating to July 1, 2001. The office also files military discharge papers (DD-214), assumed business name, partnership and incorporation instruments, and gives oaths to notaries.

Whatever sits in these books is what a title searcher will find. Look first, and ask the office about anything odd you see, such as an easement or an unreleased lien.

Deeds are searchable at martinrod.org, with records back to 1771. A separate online service takes vital record orders.

An hour in the index pays off if you inherited the house or have held it for decades.

  • Search under your name and under the previous owner's name.
  • Match the legal description on the latest deed to the tax record.
  • Watch for old deeds of trust with no release after them.
  • Note any plat or state right of way plan that touches the lot.

The county's fee sheet follows the statewide schedule, and amounts can change. Call about the total before you mail a payment, and write money orders to Martin County Register of Deeds.

Selected Martin County recording charges
ServiceCharge
Deed or other instrument, pages 1 to 15$26
Pages beyond 15$4 each
Deed of trust, pages 1 to 35$64
Plat or map (18 x 24)$21.00 a page
State right of way plans$21.00 first page, $5.00 after
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 after
Uncertified photocopy$0.25 a page
Deed excise tax$2.00 per $1000 of price
Cancellation or satisfactionNo fee
Extra instrument within one document$10.00 each

A re-recorded instrument costs the same as the original unless pages were added, and each added page is $4.

Paper signed on or after July 1, 2002 has to meet the layout standard in G.S. 161-10. Miss it and the office adds $25.00 to the recording charge.

  • Letter or legal paper, 8 1/2 inches wide.
  • Three inches left blank at the head of page one, with half an inch on the other edges.
  • Black on white, type no smaller than 9 points, printed on one face.
  • The words naming the instrument type, printed above everything else on page one.

Blanks and corrections may be inked by hand, and exhibits face the same standard. What counts is the day the paper was signed, not the day it arrives.

The seller does. The county's sheet gives $2.00 per $1000 of purchase price, and the statute expresses the same thing as $1.00 for each $500 or part of $500.

The register takes it when the deed is filed and splits it between the county general fund and the state. The county may retain 2 percent of the state portion.

The settlement statement prints the dollar amount on the seller's side, beside the loan payoff and any tax balance. No deed gets filed until the tax is paid.

sections.h2: Why filing order matters on a Williamston sale
sections.html:
Under G.S. 47-18 a conveyance, an option, a lease over three years or a right of first refusal gains force over lien creditors and paying purchasers only through registration. Martin County land registers here, whatever the owner's address.

If a creditor's judgment is filed ahead of your buyer's deed, the buyer can rank behind it. Attorneys avoid that by filing as soon as funds are confirmed.

  • Mail or deliver the signed deed with any lender release in a single packet.
  • Enclose the recording fee and the excise tax.
  • Get the book and page reference after recording.

Besides land records, the office issues marriage licenses and certified vital records. Heirs selling an inherited house often need the second kind. A certified copy of a birth, death or marriage record costs $10.00, and the county limits who may request one: the person named, a spouse, parents, siblings, children, grandchildren or grandparents, an authorized agent or attorney, or someone who can prove a legal need tied to a personal or property right.

An executor or heir usually brings proof of the relationship or a document showing legal authority. Uncertified copies are open to the public at $0.25 a page.

sections.h2: Tax bills, due dates and interest
sections.html:
Recording a deed does not change the tax bill. Bills for real and personal property go out in July or August with a September 1 due date. Payment without interest runs through January 5, and the deadline moves to the next business day if January 5 falls on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday.

A 2 percent penalty starts January 6, and interest of three-fourths of one percent accrues monthly after that. The collector must also advertise unpaid real estate tax in the local newspaper from March 1 to June 30, and the taxpayer pays extra for that notice.

The collector is at 305 East Main Street, Room 125, weekdays 8 AM to 5 PM, phone 252-789-4360. Ask for a written payoff before closing so the bill can come out of your proceeds.

Martin County has about 21,601 people as of mid-2025, down 2.0 percent since April 2020, and 11,071 housing units. Owners occupy 66.8 percent of homes, and the median home value is $109,700 (2020 to 2024).

With values this modest, deferred repairs can make a traditional lender balk. A cash buyer can purchase the house as it stands, repairs untouched, and close once title is clear. Have your attorney run the land records early so any uncancelled deed of trust gets released before closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Martin County register of deeds?
faqs.a: In the Martin County Governmental Building in Williamston, on the first floor. The county prints (252) 789-4320 for record questions.

faqs.q: How far back do Martin County land records go?
faqs.a: To 1771. The index of recorded instruments starts that year, and deeds are searchable at martinrod.org.

faqs.q: What is the Martin County fee for a deed of trust?
faqs.a: $64 through page 35, plus $4 per additional page or fraction. A plain deed costs $26 through page 15.

faqs.q: Does Martin County charge for recording a mortgage satisfaction?
faqs.a: No. Cancellations, certificates of satisfaction and notices of satisfaction all carry no fee.

faqs.q: Who pays Martin County's deed excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller, at $2.00 per $1000 of price, collected as the deed is filed.
